From today's featured article
The derailed train on the tracks
There was a disruption of train services on the East–West Line (EWL) of Singapore's Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) system on 25 September 2024. An axle box on a Kawasaki C151 train dislodged, derailing the train (pictured) and damaging the track and equipment between Clementi and Dover stations. More than 2 million commuters were affected, and shuttle train services and bus-bridging services were provided during restoration works. Full services resumed on 1 October. This was the worst breakdown in the MRT network's history. The Land Transport Authority concluded that the failure began with degraded grease in an axle bearing, which led to overheating and fire damage to the chevron springs. The Transport Safety Investigation Bureau found that fixing a "Null ID" error could have identified the affected train and prevented the incident. The rail operator, SMRT, was subsequently fined S$2.4 million (US$1.8 million) and the C151 trains were withdrawn from service by September 2025. (Full article...)

Did you know ...
Choctawhatchee beach mouse
... that the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service considers Topsail Hill Preserve State Park a genetic "reservoir" for the endangered Choctawhatchee beach mouse (example pictured)?
... that the Epic of Samba Gueladio has been interpreted as both glorifying violence against slaves and celebrating alliances across ethnicities?
... that Jasmine Wong's stage name refers to the Finnish word for 'blind'?
... that the construction of South Australia's new Parliament House in Adelaide began in 1885, but its eastern half was not completed until 1939?
... that Victor Amalraj captained three professional football clubs based in Kolkata?
... that fewer than one in fifteen residents of China live in the western 64 percent of the country?
... that Bahrija Nuri Hadžić was criticised by supporters of the Serbian Orthodox Church for her portrayal of Salome?
... that villages in India along the border with Bangladesh have protested against a proposed border fence that would leave them inside Indian territory, but beyond the fence?
... that one of Clint Reilly's clients called him "Satan"?

Tacitus
275 – After the assassination of Aurelian, Tacitus (depicted) was chosen by the Senate to succeed him as Roman emperor.
1066 – Harold Godwinson defeated King Harald III of Norway and his English ally Tostig Godwinson at the Battle of Stamford Bridge, ending the last Norse invasion of the British Isles.
1775 – American Revolutionary War: Ethan Allen and a small force of American and Quebec militia failed to capture the city of Montreal from British forces.
1800 – French Revolutionary Wars: After U.S. ships became involved, French forces abandoned their invasion of the Batavian island of Curaçao.
